title: The YM2203 registers
covers: the registers of the YM2203 as Yamaha's data sheet describes them, and MAME's handling of each

rows.text: Addresses $00 to $05 generate the frequency of the square wave sound source.
Addresses 00 to 05 are listed in a table headed READ I WRITE DATA, the I being a doubtful glyph.
The same heading names reading as well as writing; the I between READ and WRITE is a doubtful glyph.
Per channel the table has a Fine Tune and a Coarse Tune register, and its comment column names Channel-A, Channel-B and Channel-C Tone Period.
MAME forms each channel's tone period from register 2n as the low 8 bits and the low 4 bits of register 2n+1 as bits 8 to 11.
Address $06 generates the frequency of the noise source.
The capture's comment for register 06 is Noise Period.
The capture's table lists address 06.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME reads the noise period from the low 5 bits of register 0x06.
Address $07 controls the input and output of the I/O ports and the output of musical sound and noise.
The table labels register 07 with IN/OUT, IOB IOA, /Noise and /Tone, garbled in the capture, and the comment column says /ENABLE.
The capture's table lists address 07.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME reads bit 7 of register 0x07 as the output flag of I/O port B and bit 6 as that of port A.
MAME's ch_tone_enable_n reads bit choffs of register 0x07 and ch_noise_enable_n reads bit 3 plus choffs, choffs being the channel offset it is given.
Addresses $08 to $0A control sound volume; either a fixed volume (programmable) or a variable volume system can be selected.
The table labels each of these registers M Level, the M being doubtful, and the comments name Channel-A, Channel-B and Channel-C Amplitude.
Addresses 08 to 0A are listed in the address column of the READ I WRITE DATA table, whose heading is quoted at 0x00..0x05.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME reads bit 4 of each register as the envelope enable of its channel and bits 3 to 0 as its amplitude.
Addresses $0B and $0C control the envelope cycle of the variable sound volume system.
The table labels register 0B Fine Tune, the f of the capture's f'ine being doubtful, and the comment column says Envelop Period.
The capture's table lists address 0B.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME forms the 16-bit envelope period from register 0x0B as the low byte and register 0x0C as the high byte.
The capture's table labels register 0C Coarse Tune.
The capture's table lists address 0C.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME forms the 16-bit envelope period from register 0x0B as the low byte and register 0x0C as the high byte.
Address $0D specifies the envelope shape of the variable sound volume system.
The table's label for register 0D is garbled in the capture and its comment column says Envelop Shape/Cycle.
The capture's table lists address 0D.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
MAME reads bit 3 of register 0x0D as continue, bit 2 as attack, bit 1 as alternate and bit 0 as hold.
A write to register 0x0D also sets the envelope state counter to 0.
Addresses $0E and $0F are 8 bit general-purpose input and output ports.
The table labels registers 0E and 0F 1/0 Port-A and 1/0 Port-B, the 1/0 being a capture reading of I/O, and the comment says 1/0 Port Date.
Addresses 0E and 0F are listed in the address column of the READ I WRITE DATA table, whose heading is quoted at 0x00..0x05.
The table of that heading, READ I WRITE DATA, covers reading as well as writing; the I is a doubtful glyph (heading quoted at 0x00..0x05).
Register 0x0E reads through the port A callback when bit 6 of 0x07 is 0, register 0x0F through port B's when bit 7 is 0, else the stored byte.
A write of 0x0E also calls the port A write callback when bit 6 of 0x07 is 1; a write of 0x0F calls port B's when bit 7 is 1.
Address $21 holds test information, always set to 0, the capture reading the 0 as O.
Address 21 is listed in the address column of the WRITE DATA table, heading quoted at 0x21, with the label TEST and the comment LSI TEST DATA.
Addresses $24 to $26 give the set time of Timers A and B.
The comment for register 24 is most significant bits of TIMER-A, its leading figure, read B in the capture, being doubtful.
Address 24 is listed in the address column of the WRITE DATA table, heading quoted at 0x21, with the label TIMER-A.
MAME forms the value of timer A from register 0x24 as bits 9 to 2 and the low 2 bits of register 0x25 as bits 1 to 0.
The comment for register 25 is 2 least significant bits of TIMER-A.
Address 25, read 2S in the capture, is listed in the address column of the WRITE DATA table, heading quoted at 0x21, under a garbled TIMER-A label.
MAME forms the value of timer A from register 0x24 as bits 9 to 2 and the low 2 bits of register 0x25 as bits 1 to 0.
The comment for register 26 is TIMER-B DATA.
Address 26 is listed in the address column of the WRITE DATA table, heading quoted at 0x21, with the label TIMER-B.
MAME takes the value of timer B from the whole byte of register 0x26.
Address $27 controls the operation of Timers A and B, and sets the third channel mode of the FM sound source.
Address 27 is listed in the WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) with labels MODE, RESET, ENABLE and LOAD, the last three followed by B and A.
The comment for address 27 is TIMER-A/B control and 3 channel mode.
A write to address $27 controls the operation of Timers A and B.
A write to address $27 sets the third channel mode of the FM sound source.
MAME reads bits 1-0 of register 0x27 as the load of timers B and A, bits 3-2 as their enable and bits 5-4 as their flag reset.
MAME reads bits 7 and 6 of register 0x27 as the mode: the value 2 is CSM and any nonzero value is the multi-frequency mode.
MAME does not store a write of register 0x27 at once: the device defers it with a scheduler synchronize call.
Address 28, read 2B in the capture, is listed in the WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) with the labels SLOT and CH.
The comment for address 28 is Key-ON/OFF.
MAME takes the low 2 bits of register 0x28 as the channel, skips the key event for channel 3, and takes bits 7 to 4 as the operator mask.
Addresses $2D to $2F specify the dividing number of the input clock; 2 through 6 are for the FM sound source, 1 through 4 for the square wave one.
The capture's table lists address 2D.
The comment for address 2D is Set pre-scaler.
MAME sets the prescale to 6 when 0x2D is written to the address port; the data write then stores the byte in the register array.
The capture's table lists address 2E.
The comment for address 2E is Selection of the dividing numbers of 1/3 and 1/6.
MAME sets the prescale to 3 when 0x2E is written to the address port while the prescale is 6; the data write stores the byte.
The capture's table lists address 2F.
The comment for address 2F is Set a divider to the dividing number of 1/2.
MAME sets the prescale to 2 when 0x2F is written to the address port; the data write then stores the byte in the register array.
Addresses $30 to $3E control detune and multiple, which set tones and the relationship between the fundamental wave and the harmonic.
The WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) lists addresses 30 and 3E with the labels DT and MULTI, the capture reading I / DT MULTI.
The comment for addresses 30 to 3E is Detune / Multiple.
The comment adds that addresses 33, 37 and 3B are empty.
MAME reads bits 6 to 4 of each register as the detune and bits 3 to 0 as the multiple of its operator.
Addresses $40 to $4E give the total level, which becomes the modulation index of the sound volume and modulation wave of the modulated wave.
The WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) lists addresses 40 and 4E with the label TL, the capture reading I / TL.
The comment for addresses 40 to 4E is Total Level.
The comment adds that addresses 43, 47 and 4B are empty.
MAME reads bits 6 to 0 of each register as the total level of its operator.
MAME reads the total level of its operator n at 0x40 plus n plus n/3, in integer division.
Addresses $50 to $5E: Key Scale controls the rate of change of A, D, S and R according to keyboard information; Attack rate gives the rate of change at attack.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds two entries the capture reads so and SE, doubtful OCR glyphs; the label line reads KS~ AR.
The comment for these addresses is Key Scale / Attack Rate.
The comment adds that addresses 53, S7 and SB are empty; the capture's S7 and SB are doubtful OCR glyphs.
MAME reads bits 7 and 6 of each register as the key scale rate and bits 4 to 0 as the attack rate of its operator.
Addresses $60 to $6E: Decay Rate shows the rate of change of the envelope at the time of decay.
The WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) lists addresses 60 and 6E with the label DR.
The comment for addresses 60 to 6E is Decay Rate.
The comment adds that addresses 63, 67 and 68 are empty; the capture's 68 is a doubtful OCR glyph.
MAME reads bits 4 to 0 of each register as the decay rate of its operator.
Addresses $70 to $7E: Sustain Rate shows the rate of change of the envelope at the time of sustain.
The WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) lists addresses 70 and 7E with the label SR.
The comment for addresses 70 to 7E is Sustain Rate.
The comment adds that addresses 73, 77 and 7B are empty.
MAME reads bits 4 to 0 of each register as the sustain rate of its operator.
Addresses from $80: Sustain level shows the level of the shift from decay to sustain; Release rate shows the rate of change at release.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds two entries the capture reads BO and BE, doubtful OCR glyphs; the label line reads SL RR.
The comment for these addresses is Sustain Level / Release Rate.
The comment adds that addresses B3, B7 and BB are empty; the capture's letters are doubtful OCR glyphs.
MAME reads bits 7 to 4 of each register as the sustain level and bits 3 to 0 as the release rate of its operator.
Addresses $90 to $9E generate the envelope including the repeat pattern similar to that of the square wave sound source.
The WRITE DATA table (heading at 0x21) lists addresses 90 and 9E with the label SSG-EG, the capture reading 0 SSG-EG.
The comment for addresses 90 to 9E is SSG-Type Envelop Control.
The comment adds that addresses 93, 97 and 9B are empty.
MAME reads bit 3 of each register as the SSG-EG enable and bits 2 to 0 as the SSG-EG mode of its operator.
Addresses $A0 to $A6 give the key-code (F-number) of each channel; the capture reads the first address $AO.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds three entries the capture reads AO, Al and A2, doubtful OCR glyphs, with the label F-Num. 1.
The comment line after the one for 90 to 9E reads F-Numbers / BLOCK; the capture shows no address beside it.
MAME reads a channel's block and frequency as a 14-bit word: bits 5 to 0 of its 0xA4 register shifted above all 8 bits of its 0xA0 register.
A write to 0xA0..0xA2 is stored and copies the latch byte (internal register 0xB8) into the register 4 above it.
A write whose address has 3 in its low two bits (0xA3, 0xA7, 0xAB, 0xAF) is not stored in the register array.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds three entries the capture reads A4, AS and A6, AS being doubtful.
The label line for these addresses reads L BLOCK F-Num. 2, the L being doubtful.
MAME reads bits 5 to 0 of a channel's 0xA4 register as the six high bits of its 14-bit block and frequency word.
A write to 0xA4..0xA6 stores its low 6 bits in a latch that the three channels share.
A write whose address has 3 in its low two bits (0xA3, 0xA7, 0xAB, 0xAF) is not stored in the register array.
Addresses $A8 to $AE give the key-code (F-number) of three channels when set to the special mode.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds three entries the capture reads AB, A9 and AA, AB being doubtful; the label line reads 3CH * F-Num. 1.
The capture has the two comment lines 3CH-3slot and F-Numbers / BLOCK, with no address beside them.
When 0x27 bits 7 and 6 are not 0, MAME gives channel 2's operators at register offsets 6, 2 and 10 the frequency of 0xA8, 0xA9 and 0xAA.
MAME builds a special-mode frequency from bits 5 to 0 of 0xAC plus n, shifted above all 8 bits of 0xA8 plus n; n is a group offset.
A write to 0xA8..0xAA is stored and copies the latch byte (internal register 0xB9) into the register 4 above it.
A write whose address has 3 in its low two bits (0xA3, 0xA7, 0xAB, 0xAF) is not stored in the register array.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds three entries, which the capture reads AC, AD and AE.
The label lines read Vl3CH * 3CH * and BLOCK F-Num. 2, the Vl being doubtful.
MAME builds a special-mode frequency from bits 5 to 0 of 0xAC plus n, shifted above all 8 bits of 0xA8 plus n; n is a group offset.
A write to 0xAC..0xAE stores its low 6 bits in a latch of its own, apart from the one of 0xA4..0xA6.
A write whose address has 3 in its low two bits (0xA3, 0xA7, 0xAB, 0xAF) is not stored in the register array.
Addresses $B0 to $B2 give the modulation system (connection) of the FM modulation and the factor of the feedback FM (self-feedback); the capture reads $BO and $82.
The address column of the WRITE DATA table holds three entries the capture reads BO, Bl and B2; the label line reads L FB CONNECT.
The capture's line reads Self-Feedback / Connection and then YM2203.
MAME reads bits 5 to 3 of each register as the feedback and bits 2 to 0 as the algorithm of its channel.
MAME reads the feedback and algorithm of channel n at 0xB0 plus the channel offset, which is n when the chip is not an OPNA.
